newsitem.title: USA: USDA analyst sees small Brazil soybean shipments.
newsitem.headline: USDA analyst sees small Brazil soybean shipments.

text.p: A top U.S. Agriculture Department soybean analyst predicted Brazilian soybean shipments to the United States would be small and may well be rerouted to another destination after today's market drop.
CBOT July soybean futures touched down the 30-cent-per-bushel trading limit in late dealings amid fast trading on news Brazil soybeans were being shipped to the U.S.
"If there is any delivered we're talking about small quantities," said James Matthews, chairman of USDA's World Agricultural Outlook Board for soybeans.
He reckoned the price spreads made sense when the beans were booked and do not make sense now.

"It probably makes it unlikely we'll ever see those beans hit the U.S. shores. There would be a lot of interested buyers at 30 cents off the price of soybeans. It makes it a lot easier to negotiate an alternative seller or buyer," Matthews said.
